quests.hint: Separate the cause from the effects it produced, and watch for the reaction that responds to the effect.
quests.explanation: Leaving milk out is the cause, spoiling is the effect, and pouring it away is his reaction. Buying a replacement follows because the old carton is gone. Each event exists because of the one before.
sentences: A quick walk to the corner shop got him a fresh one.
Wei left the milk on the counter during a long afternoon call.
By evening, the carton smelled sour.
Wei poured the whole thing down the sink.
quests.instruction: Put the events in the order that makes the story coherent.

quests.hint: A new rule usually follows a painful lesson.
quests.explanation: The blackout triggers the shutdown, and the shutdown explains the lost report. Oksana's rule is a response to that loss, so it can only come after it.
sentences: A storm knocked out power to the office building.
When the lights returned, a colleague found her unsaved report had vanished.
The manager, Oksana, asked everyone to save their work every ten minutes.
The servers shut down without warning.
quests.instruction: Sort the sentences into the sequence that makes sense.

quests.hint: Follow the chain: which change made the next change possible?
quests.explanation: The lane changes commuter behavior, and fewer cars mean smoother roads. Reliable buses eventually lead planners to adjust the timetable. Each effect becomes the cause of the next.
sentences: Buses on that corridor began arriving closer to schedule.
Traffic thinned out on the main street beside it.
More people chose to cycle to work along that route.
The transit authority shortened its published timetable within the year.
The city painted a protected lane along Harbor Road.
quests.instruction: Reconstruct the story so that every event follows from the one before it.
quests.plotStructure: Initial Change, Behavior Shift, Ripple Effect, Improvement, Policy Change

quests.hint: Ask what caused the damage and what the character did about it.
quests.explanation: The drop causes the crack, and the crack gives Jiho a reason to visit the kiosk. The repair is the resolution of the problem the accident created.
sentences: A crack ran diagonally across the screen.
Jiho took it to a repair kiosk at the mall.
Jiho dropped his phone on the tile floor.
The technician fitted a new screen in twenty minutes.
quests.instruction: Reorder the sentences to produce the most logical version of events.

quests.hint: What action caused the plant's condition, and who advised a change?
quests.explanation: Constant watering keeps the soil soaked, and soaked soil damages the roots, which shows in the leaves. The advice only makes sense once the damage is visible.
sentences: The soil never had a chance to dry out.
A nursery worker advised her to water only when the top inch felt dry.
Yellow leaves began to droop over the pot.
Ms. Petrova watered her fern every morning.
quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences into a coherent account of what happened.

quests.hint: Look for a decision, its immediate effect, and the wider result.
quests.explanation: The early deadline creates room for feedback, feedback improves the essays, and better essays raise the average. The department's adoption is a consequence of visible success.
sentences: Final essays improved noticeably.
The class average on the assignment rose compared with last term.
Mr. Adeyemi asked students to submit drafts a week early.
Students received feedback while there was still time to revise.
The department adopted the early-draft rule in all sections.
quests.instruction: Rebuild the sequence from beginning to outcome.

quests.hint: A late-morning consequence often traces back to a problem that happened much earlier.
quests.explanation: The dead phone is the root cause. It leads to waking late, then to skipping breakfast, and the hunger during the lecture is the final effect.
sentences: By mid-morning, her stomach was growling through the lecture.
Sana's phone died overnight, so her morning alarm never rang.
Sana skipped breakfast to catch the bus.
Sana woke up forty minutes late.
quests.instruction: Restore the story's natural progression.

quests.hint: Follow the smoke: what did it cause, and who reacted to that?
quests.explanation: The unattended oil is the cause of the smoke, the alarm is triggered by the smoke, and the neighbors react to the alarm. Bruno's apology and open windows are his reaction to the whole situation.
sentences: Bruno left a pan of oil heating on the stove while he answered the door.
Neighbors knocked to make sure he was safe.
Bruno apologized and propped the windows open.
The smoke set off the alarm in the hallway.
The oil began to smoke.
quests.instruction: Reconstruct the story so that every event follows from the one before it.

quests.hint: Notice how a small trigger changed what the character eventually did.
quests.explanation: The coupon gives her a reason to visit, and being there exposes her to something new. That discovery changes her purchase and, over time, her habits.
sentences: Pilar visited the shop before it expired.
The bookshop mailed Pilar a coupon for twenty percent off.
Pilar left with two poetry books instead of the novel she had come for.
These days she attends the shop's monthly reading night.
While browsing, she noticed a shelf of poetry she had never seen.
quests.instruction: Arrange the events so each action logically leads to the next.
quests.plotStructure: Trigger, Action, Discovery, Outcome, Long-term Effect

quests.hint: Look for the event that makes each later action necessary.
quests.explanation: The unlocked bicycle makes theft possible, and the theft makes reporting necessary. The footage is offered as a response to the report.
sentences: Cedric left his bicycle unlocked outside the library.
Cedric reported the theft at the front desk.
The librarian offered to show him the security footage.
When he came out, it was gone.
quests.instruction: Put the events in the order that makes the story coherent.

quests.hint: A shortage in the store has a reason further back than the store itself.
quests.explanation: The road closure blocks deliveries, and missing deliveries cause the shortage. The sign is a management response to a shortage that has already appeared.
sentences: Delivery trucks could not reach the loading dock.
The supermarket's shelves ran low on bread.
Heavy snow closed the highway near the warehouse.
The manager put up a sign asking customers to limit their purchases.
quests.instruction: Place the events in the order they must occur.

quests.hint: What began as a small task grew into something else. Find the point where each new development becomes possible.
quests.explanation: The newsletter creates awareness, the sign-up creates the route, and the route creates the meeting. The tea visits grow from that meeting, and the daughter's letter is the last consequence.
sentences: Their daughter later wrote to thank the food bank for the company he gave them.
His route took him past an elderly couple who rarely saw visitors.
He began staying for a cup of tea.
A newsletter mentioned that the food bank was short of drivers.
Retiree Anselm signed up for Saturday deliveries.
quests.instruction: Decide which event comes first, and build the sequence from there.

quests.hint: Which sentence describes what caused the flicker?
quests.explanation: The cup's placement makes the spill possible, and the spill causes the damage. Turning the laptop off and seeking repair is the reaction.
sentences: Ola switched the laptop off and took it to a repair shop.
Coffee seeped under the keys, and the screen began to flicker.
Her elbow knocked the cup over.
Ola set her coffee cup next to her laptop.
quests.instruction: Reorder the sentences to produce the most logical version of events.

quests.hint: Praise can cause action. Follow how that action grows.
quests.explanation: The compliment motivates Tunde to volunteer. His volunteering builds a reputation, and the reputation eventually earns him a formal role.
sentences: Encouraged, Tunde offered to make the visuals for the whole team.
His manager added visual reporting to his job description.
A coworker praised Tunde's hand-drawn charts during a meeting.
By spring, others came to him whenever they needed a graphic.
quests.instruction: Rebuild the sequence from beginning to outcome.
quests.plotStructure: Recognition, Initiative, Reputation, Promotion of Role

quests.hint: Track how a public decision changes what people choose to do.
quests.explanation: The dry weather leads to the rule, and the rule causes brown lawns. Residents adapt with different plants, and the store responds to their new demand.
sentences: Residents began planting drought-tolerant flowers.
The garden center rearranged its shelves to feature them.
The council limited garden watering to two evenings a week.
Lawns turned brown across the neighborhood.
The town reported an unusually dry summer.
quests.instruction: Order these sentences so the situation develops logically.
quests.plotStructure: Condition, Policy, Effect, Adaptation, Market Response

quests.hint: The error described at the start is the one the later sentences uncover.
quests.explanation: The mislabeling is the hidden cause, the wrong spoonful is the action based on it, and the salty taste is the consequence. Fixing the labels is the correction.
sentences: Renata spooned what she believed was sugar into her tea.
While cleaning the pantry, Renata put the labels back on the wrong jars.
Renata peeled the labels off and stuck them on the correct jars.
The first sip was so salty that she winced.
quests.instruction: Work out the order in which these events unfold.

quests.hint: Effort produces results, and results produce reactions from others.
quests.explanation: The repeated practice leads to improvement, and improvement produces confidence at the recital. The audience's reaction is the final effect.
sentences: Ivan spent twenty minutes each evening on the hardest passage of his recital piece.
The audience applauded longest after that piece.
The passage gradually became smooth.
At the recital, it no longer made his hands shake.
quests.instruction: Arrange the events so each action logically leads to the next.

quests.hint: A mistake in communication has effects that spread through many people.
quests.explanation: The wrong list causes the confusion, the confusion sends people to the wrong place, and the note then redirects them. The late arrivals are a consequence of the detour, and the new habit is what the organizer learns.
sentences: The organizer sent the venue change to the wrong mailing list.
They found the doors locked and a note taped to the glass.
The organizer now checks the list twice before sending any announcement.
Half of the attendees went to the old hall.
Some drove across town and arrived after the talk had begun.
quests.instruction: Place the events in the order they must occur.

quests.hint: Skin damage takes time to show. What follows the damage?
quests.explanation: The exposure causes the burn, but the burn only becomes visible later. The aloe treats it, and the shirt is a longer-term response to the same problem.
sentences: Kwabena smoothed aloe gel across them.
Kwabena spent the whole afternoon at the beach without sunscreen.
By night, his shoulders were bright red.
The next day, he wore a long-sleeved shirt to work.
quests.instruction: Put the events in the order that makes the story coherent.

quests.hint: Ask how an easier system changes behavior and how the change affects costs.
quests.explanation: Convenient bins change habits, and better sorting creates more recycling and less garbage. With less garbage, fewer pickups are needed.
sentences: The volume of recycling collected doubled in a month.
Residents found it easier to sort their trash.
The landlord reduced the number of general-waste pickups.
The apartment complex placed color-coded bins in the lobby.
quests.instruction: Decide which event comes first, and build the sequence from there.

quests.hint: Identify the observation that prompts a change, then follow the change's effects.
quests.explanation: The observation is the problem that motivates the coach's decision. The tougher ending prepares the players, and the improved finish produces the win.
sentences: The coach changed practice so the toughest drill came last.
In the next match, they scored twice in the closing minutes.
Coach Delgado noticed his team lost most games in the final ten minutes.
Players grew used to working hard while tired.
The team won its first game of the season.
quests.instruction: Order these sentences so the situation develops logically.

quests.hint: A business change is usually a reaction to what customers experienced.
quests.explanation: Selling out is the trigger, disappointment is the effect, and the second batch is the owner's response. More stock later in the morning naturally increases sales.
sentences: Sales rose noticeably in the late morning.
Customers who arrived later left disappointed.
The bakery ran out of croissants by 8 a.m.
The owner started baking a second batch at dawn.
quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences into a coherent account of what happened.

quests.hint: A request only appears after a problem has been noticed.
quests.explanation: The late practice disturbs the neighbor, and the note is her reaction. Leon changes his schedule in response to the note.
sentences: Leon moved his sessions to the afternoon.
Leon started drum practice at ten each night.
His downstairs neighbor could not sleep.
She left a polite note on his door.
quests.instruction: Arrange the events so each action logically leads to the next.

quests.hint: Identify the event that forces a change of plan, then the problem that the change creates.
quests.explanation: The strike prevents travel, and the video link is the workaround. The workaround has its own weakness, which the technician fixes.
sentences: The organizers arranged for her to speak by video link.
A technician replaced the microphone, and the audience finally heard her clearly.
Poor audio made the first minutes hard to follow.
A regional strike halted all trains to the capital.
The keynote speaker could not reach the conference in person.
quests.instruction: Reorder the sentences to produce the most logical version of events.

quests.hint: Which event is the origin of the crowd?
quests.explanation: The typing error creates the bargain, the bargain attracts people, and the crowd draws the manager's attention. Correcting the tag is the response to what she discovers.
sentences: A clerk typed 9.99 instead of 99.99 on a jacket's price tag.
The manager saw the crowd and checked the tag.
She corrected the price and apologized to the people waiting.
Shoppers noticed the bargain and formed a line.
quests.instruction: Sort the sentences into the sequence that makes sense.

quests.hint: Trace the complaint back to the change that caused it.
quests.explanation: The change introduces the fault, and the fault produces confusion for users. The rollback and apology follow only once the source of the complaints is known.
sentences: Customers complained about mismatched invoices.
The team rolled back the change and sent an apology notice.
Reports began showing dates in the wrong order.
A developer changed the date format in the company's app.
quests.instruction: Decide which event comes first, and build the sequence from there.

quests.hint: A setback can create an unexpected advantage. Trace how.
quests.explanation: The delay leads to the missed train, which leads to the hotel. The hotel morning provides study time that improves his calm, so the story ends with the benefit no one planned.
sentences: Kiran walked into the interview the next day calm instead of rushed.
Free time at breakfast let him review his interview notes.
Kiran's flight was delayed by three hours.
Kiran missed the last train from the airport.
Kiran booked a night at a nearby hotel.
quests.instruction: Place the events in the order they must occur.

quests.hint: The final action responds to the problem that developed slowly.
quests.explanation: The closed window traps moisture, moisture causes mold, and the mold prompts Jorge to change his habits. The fix targets the original cause.
sentences: Moisture collected on the walls.
Dark spots of mold appeared near the ceiling.
The bathroom window stayed shut all winter.
Jorge bought a fan and began opening the window after showers.
quests.instruction: Put the events in the order that makes the story coherent.

quests.hint: Follow how an accident leads to an opportunity.
quests.explanation: The mistake places Marisol in an unfamiliar village, and lunch there leads to a meeting. The supplier relationship grows out of that chance encounter.
sentences: Marisol stopped for lunch at a café she had never heard of.
Marisol misread the map and took a wrong turn.
The road led her to a small lakeside village.
The owner later became the supplier for the shop she was about to open.
quests.instruction: Order these sentences so the situation develops logically.

quests.hint: Look for the change that starts a chain reaching from one business to another.
quests.explanation: The budget cut changes how staff work, and the changed behavior reduces demand for supplies. The supplier's lost income leads to discounts.
sentences: The office needed far fewer printer cartridges.
A firm cut its printing budget.
It offered discounts to attract new customers.
Employees began emailing documents instead of printing them.
The cartridge supplier lost a large client.
quests.instruction: Arrange the events so each action logically leads to the next.
quests.plotStructure: Decision, Behavior Change, Demand Shift, Loss, Response
